question: For the patient who has the highest Ig A within the normal range, what is his or her diagnosis?
evidence: highest Ig A within the normal range refers to MAX(IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500);
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0 FROM (SELECT patientData.Diagnosis AS c0, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY labData.IGA DESC) AS __r FROM Patient AS patientData INNER JOIN Laboratory AS labData ON patientData.ID = labData.ID WHERE labData.IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT patientData.Diagnosis FROM Patient AS patientData INNER JOIN Laboratory AS labData ON patientData.ID = labData.ID WHERE labData.IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500 ORDER BY labData.IGA DESC LIMIT 1

b.request: Find the diagnosis of every patient whose Laboratory IGA value equals the maximum IGA value among records with IGA between 80 and 500, returning all patients tied at that maximum
b.sql: SELECT DISTINCT P.Diagnosis FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA > 80 AND IGA < 500)

c.sql: SELECT DISTINCT P.Diagnosis FROM Patient P INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA BETWEEN 80 AND 500)

d.request: For the patient(s) with the highest IgA within the normal range (IgA between 80 and 500), what is their diagnosis? If several patients tie for that highest IgA value, return the diagnoses for all of them.
d.sql: SELECT DISTINCT P.Diagnosis FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.IGA = (SELECT MAX(IGA) FROM Laboratory WHERE IGA > 80 AND IGA < 500)
